rules.title: Ban on retaliatory termination, rent increase, or change in tenancy terms
rules.requirement: A landlord may not threaten or retaliate against you, for example with a termination notice, rent increase or major change in lease terms, because you reported code violations, took legal action under housing laws, complained in writing, or organized or joined a tenants' union. A termination notice (other than for nonpayment), a rent increase, or a major change in terms within six months of that activity is presumed to be retaliation, and you can recover 1 to 3 months' rent or your actual damages, whichever is greater, plus attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: 6-month rebuttable presumption of reprisal; damages of 1–3 months' rent or actual damages, whichever is greater
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants of residential premises in Massachusetts. Applies to any person or agent who threatens or takes reprisals.
rules.exemptions: Termination notices for nonpayment of rent do not trigger the presumption.
rules.penalty: Damages of at least one month's rent and up to three months' rent, or actual damages, whichever is greater, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees. Any lease waiver is void.
rules.reason: Only one candidate, from official statute text. It is kept as a single record for the anti-retaliation statute; the record does not give an effective date.
